entities.name: George of Polentz
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
George of Polentz (died 1550-05-08) was a pivotal figure in the early spread of the Protestant Reformation, specifically in the Teutonic Order State and the subsequent Duchy of Prussia. As Bishop of Samland and Pomesania, he became the first Catholic bishop to formally convert to Lutheranism and implement the Reformation within his diocese, preceding even the secularization of the Teutonic Order. His actions under Duke Albert of Prussia were instrumental in establishing Prussia as the first officially Lutheran state, fundamentally altering the religious and political landscape of Central Europe in the 16th century.

Born to a noble family in Saxony, Polentz initially pursued a career in law, serving as a legal advisor at the Roman Rota, the highest appellate tribunal of the Catholic Church. His ecclesiastical career advanced rapidly, culminating in his appointment as Bishop of Samland in 1519 and administrator of the Diocese of Pomesania in 1523. Initially resistant to the nascent Lutheran teachings, Polentz was swayed by the theological arguments of Andreas Osiander and the personal conviction of Duke Albert. On December 25, 1525, Polentz publicly preached a sermon in Königsberg Cathedral advocating for evangelical doctrine, a moment often cited as the official introduction of the Reformation into Prussia. He subsequently oversaw the implementation of Lutheran reforms, including the abolition of monastic vows, the introduction of communion in both kinds, and the marriage of clergy, setting a precedent for other German territories.
